name: Rosemary
grown_as: Rosemary, an evergreen shrub. Drawn upright with pale blue flowers, the usual form; there are prostrate forms and white, pink and deep blue flowered ones. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: An upright, bushy, evergreen shrub 60 to 150 cm high, with stiff, woody stems, grey-brown and peeling with age, densely clothed in needle-like leaves.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, but so crowded they look like a brush around the stem
leaf.outline: Needle-like, long and very narrow, 1.5 to 4 cm long and 2 to 4 mm wide
leaf.margin: Smooth, no teeth, rolled under so strongly the leaf looks like a thick needle
leaf.veins: A groove down the middle above; the midrib raised beneath
leaf.surface: Leathery, a little glossy and wrinkled above; white woolly beneath, the white showing either side of the midrib

flower.form: A two-lipped flower with a hooded top and a hanging lower lip
flower.petals: Joined; the upper lip a hood, notched at the tip; the lower lip three-lobed, its large middle lobe cupped and hanging
flower.colour: Pale blue to lilac-blue, the lower lip spotted darker
flower.centre: Two long stamens and the style arching up and out of the upper lip
flower.behind: A small green or purple-tinged, two-lipped, bell-shaped calyx, finely hairy
flower.carried: In short clusters of 2 to 10 in the leaf joints along the upper part of the shoots, sitting among the leaves; no separate spike
flower.season: March to May, and odd flowers through the year

fruit: Four small brown nutlets in each calyx; rarely noticed.
winter: Evergreen: unchanged, often with a few flowers.

leaf: a long needle-like leaf with a blunt tip
bloom: hooded upper lip, hanging lower lip spotted darker
long stamens arching up out of the hood
young: a small upright woody plant densely clothed in needle-like leaves
crop: stems thick with dark green needle-like leaves
flower: pale blue flowers in small clusters among the leaves along the upper shoots

look_alikes: Lavender has grey felted leaves and flowers in spikes on long bare stalks. Hyssop has flat, soft leaves green on both sides and dense violet-blue spikes in late summer. Westringia, sometimes sold as Australian rosemary, has leaves in rings of four and white flowers.
